title: Superficial muscles of the back and shoulder (posterior)
lab: Shoulder Joint, Scapular Muscles, and Posterior Arm
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender; surface detail added with an image model.

rows: Medial third of the superior nuchal line, external occipital protuberance, ligamentum nuchae and the spinous processes of C7 to T12.
Lateral third of the clavicle, the acromion and the spine of the scapula.
Accessory nerve (CN XI) for movement; C3 and C4 carry pain and proprioception.
Upper fibers raise the scapula, middle fibers retract it and lower fibers depress it. Upper and lower fibers together rotate the scapula upward.
hy: Injury to the accessory nerve, for example during surgery in the posterior triangle of the neck, causes a drooping shoulder and weakness raising the arm above the horizontal.

structures.name: Deltoid muscle
objects: Scapular spinal part of deltoid muscle.r

rows: Lateral third of the clavicle, the acromion and the spine of the scapula.
Abducts the arm beyond the first 15 degrees. The anterior fibers flex and medially rotate the arm; the posterior fibers extend and laterally rotate it.
hy: The axillary nerve is injured by a fracture of the surgical neck of the humerus or an anterior dislocation of the shoulder: the deltoid flattens, abduction is weak, and sensation is lost over the lateral shoulder.

rows: Spinous processes of T7 to T12, thoracolumbar fascia, iliac crest and the lower three or four ribs.
Floor of the intertubercular sulcus of the humerus.
Extends, adducts and medially rotates the arm.
hy: A lady between two majors: latissimus dorsi inserts in the floor of the intertubercular sulcus, between pectoralis major on the lateral lip and teres major on the medial lip.

rows: Long head: infraglenoid tubercle of the scapula. Lateral head: posterior humerus above the radial groove. Medial head: posterior humerus below the radial groove.
Extends the elbow. The long head helps extend and adduct the arm at the shoulder.
hy: The triceps reflex tests mainly C7.

rows: Middle facet of the greater tubercle of the humerus.
Laterally rotates the arm. Holds the head of the humerus in the glenoid cavity.
